evals.prompt: I keep thinking about building a tool that turns messy meeting notes into a weekly status report for engineering managers. I have no idea if anyone would pay for it. Can you help me figure out whether this is worth building? I've got nothing yet, just the idea.
evals.expected_output: A validation plan with typed falsifiable assumptions (value/viability first), a cheap pre-validation ladder, a Mom Test interview guide, a competitor/alternative scan, and a go/no-go brief that stops short of making the decision. Should reference founder/validation/ outputs and not offer to build the app.
expectations: Produces typed assumptions (value, viability, usability, feasibility) rather than a single verdict
Includes a Mom Test style interview guide asking about past behaviour, not hypotheticals
Names the human go/no-go boundary explicitly
Recommends the cheapest next test rather than jumping to build

evals.prompt: Here are my notes from 8 customer calls for my invoicing app for freelance designers. [pastes rambling notes] Everyone said it sounds great and several said they'd definitely use it. I think we're good to start building - thoughts?
evals.expected_output: The skill should push back on compliments-as-validation, separate interest from demand, restructure the raw notes into per-interview records with verbatim quotes and commitment levels, score the evidence via the script, and refuse to conclude 'proceed' while value/viability assumptions are untested. Should surface the case against.
expectations: Challenges 'sounds great / would use' as weak evidence
Reorganises notes into per-interview records with commitment levels
Runs or describes scripts/evidence_scorecard.py and reports a verdict band
Does not endorse 'start building' on sentiment alone

evals.prompt: should I build a niche CRM for wedding photographers? i saw a bunch of people complaining about it on reddit and i built crms before so it's easy for me
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as an idea-validation request even with casual phrasing. Distinguishes the founder's feasibility confidence from market risk, proposes the 2/20/200 ladder, maps incumbents/alternatives, designs a willingness-to-pay test, and produces a plan and go/no-go brief rather than a 'yes'.
expectations: Identifies market risk (frequent, reachable, pays) as distinct from feasibility
Proposes a cheap pre-validation ladder before building
Designs a willingness-to-pay test, not just a waitlist
Ends with a brief and next test, deferring the decision to the founder
